observations.Q2: The CacheGroup key index can silently under-represent the live keys — index() returns early for an already-indexed key so the index's 7-day TTL is never refreshed while entry TTLs restart on every cache miss (and the read-modify-write of the index is non-atomic across concurrent requests) — so once the index expires or loses an entry, flush() forgets nothing for those keys and stale content keeps being served after a create/update/delete.

observations.Q3: app/Actions/Dish/UpdateDishAction.php::execute (the unshown tail of the method that consumes and persists $data)

observations.Q2: CacheGroup's key index is never refreshed once a key is already listed (`index()` returns early on `in_array`), so the 7-day index entry expires while shorter-TTL entries are still cached and, after expiry, only keys read again get re-indexed — leaving the remaining group entries orphaned so a later `CacheGroup::flush()` silently fails to invalidate them (the same read-modify-write index is also lost under concurrent requests, and `flush()` deleting the index orphans any value a concurrent `remember()` is about to write).
observations.Q5: Must outlive the longest entry TTL used by callers, otherwise the index expires while its entries are still cached and they leak.
